items.description: The match is a bare unanchored substring: `grep -q 'delete'` fires on any command containing the word, so `git push origin feat/delete-user` and `rm delete-me.txt` are both blocked. It also misses the actual delete forms — `git push origin --delete br` matches by luck, `git push origin :br` does not match at all. The guard blocks the wrong commands and lets the colon-refspec delete through.

The comment documents calling with_retry with no arguments to retry the default allowlist read. Under `set -u` the body dereferences "$1" immediately, so a no-argument call aborts the shell with an unbound-variable error rather than running the default. A helper whose documented calling convention crashes reads `${1:-<default>}` instead.

GUARDS.md states block-secret-write covers shell redirection as well as Write and Edit, naming `cat > config.yml` as stopped. hooks.json registers that hook on the `Write|Edit` matcher only, and the script reads .tool_input.content, which a Bash call does not carry. Redirection never reaches the guard, so the documented half of its coverage does not exist.

When read_allow_patterns fails, `set -e` aborts the hook at this assignment, so it exits 1 — a hook error, after which the call proceeds. GUARDS.md:14 says a guard that cannot reach its allowlist fails closed. Failing closed means exiting 2 on that path, not letting the shell exit on the author's behalf.

block-branch-delete.sh has no suite at all — tests/hooks/ covers only block-secret-write.sh. It is the guard whose match logic is wrong in both directions, and no test would have to be clever to catch it.
The retry count lives in lib/retry.sh:9 as the loop bound and again in GUARDS.md prose as "retries twice". One value, two homes, no single source.
